newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 1.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Democrats are poised for a 32-seat landslide victory in Bangkok, boosting Chuan Leekpai's chances of becoming prime minister for a second time, according to a Bangkok Post-Ramkhamhaeng poll. Palang Dharma emerges the biggest losers. Meanwhile, rivals of the New Aspiration Party (NAP) have alleged that influential NAP "lobbyists" with military connections are intimidating northern canvassers and election candidates in a bid to secure votes for General Chavalit Yongchaiyudh. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- A long stretch of beach on Chuang Island in the Gulf of Thailand has been covered with oil from Wednesday's tanker spill. A large slick of about 800 square metres is floating just south of the island and coral near the island are under threat. (BANGKOK POST)

- A contract to build part of the subway system will be signed on Tuesday by the Metropolitan Rapid Transit Authority and Joint Venture BCKT, led by Ch Karnchang Plc. Work is expected to start early next year and take 3.5 years to complete. (BANGKOK POST)

- Prasong Panichpakdi says that attempts to link him to the Bangkok Bank of Commerce (BBC) scandal and the arrest warrant against him are a plot to destroy his image and that of his company. The chairman and managing director of Somprasong Land Plc denied he was involved in the BBC scandal as claimed by three former Somprasong employees. (BANGKOK POST)

- The National Economic and Social Development Board (NESDB) has been assigned to conduct a study on expanding the industrial area of the Map Ta Phut Industrial Estate, and to assess areas in three eastern provinces with the view of establishing further industrial zones. (BUSINESS DAY)
